LQA standard (source wording): Did the employee offer the option to order food or supply a restaurant menu?
What the system demonstrates: Capture the guest's food request or preference after staff offers food or a restaurant menu.
Evidence needed to mark: Complete conversation is needed to verify the spoken offer and any guest response; a silent menu supply requires visual evidence.

LQA standard (source wording): Did the employee offer to take the drinks order within 3 minutes of seating?
What the system demonstrates: Compare seating and offer times; surface an order-taking cue when needed.
Evidence needed to mark: Seating and offer timestamps plus complete service coverage are needed to verify the three-minute interval.

LQA standard (source wording): Did the employee show excellent product knowledge when taking the order and promote local/signature drinks, where applicable?
What the system demonstrates: Check the staff recommendation against current, approved beverage facts.
Evidence needed to mark: Current approved beverage menu and recorded staff response are needed to assess product knowledge.

LQA standard (source wording): Was the employee able to accommodate any reasonable off menu requests, or custom drink orders?
What the system demonstrates: Capture the custom request and staff response as structured interaction data.
Evidence needed to mark: Guest request, staff response, and service/order outcome are needed to confirm accommodation.

LQA standard (source wording): Did the employee offer a choice of brand/variety when taking the drink order if there was an opportunity to do so?
What the system demonstrates: Display available brands or varieties and capture the guest's selection.
Evidence needed to mark: Available menu choices and complete order-taking dialogue are needed to confirm the opportunity and offer.

LQA standard (source wording): Was the employee able to answer any questions with regard to the menu, its ingredients and allergies, where applicable?
What the system demonstrates: Capture the ingredient/allergy question and route the response for comparison with approved data.
Evidence needed to mark: Current approved menu, ingredient, and allergen source plus the staff response are needed; do not infer safety from reassurance.

LQA standard (source wording): Did the employee obtain a full and complete order (i.e. cooking instructions, accompaniments etc.)?
What the system demonstrates: Structure spoken items, cooking instructions, accompaniments, and read-back.
Evidence needed to mark: Complete dialogue and final order/POS record are needed to confirm the order was complete and correct.

LQA standard (source wording): If special dietary requirements were provided at any point during the stay, were they discreetly re-confirmed?
What the system demonstrates: Capture the discreet reconfirmation and link it to an authorized prior dietary record.
Evidence needed to mark: Authorized prior dietary record plus current interaction/audio are needed; a new disclosure does not prove prior disclosure.

LQA standard (source wording): CLARITY - Was the employee’s speech clear and use of English satisfactory, enabling engagement in two-way conversation with the guest?
What the system demonstrates: Assess speech audio clarity and transcription confidence.
Evidence needed to mark: Raw audio and human review are needed; transcript text alone cannot establish speech clarity.

LQA standard (source wording): ENGAGEMENT - Did the employees engage in a well-paced, natural (non-scripted, jargon/slang free), friendly and interested manner?
What the system demonstrates: Assess conversational pace, tone, and natural engagement.
Evidence needed to mark: Raw audio and human calibration are needed; polite words alone do not establish pace or tone.

LQA standard (source wording): GUEST'S NAME - Did the employee use the guest's name naturally and discreetly without overusing it?
What the system demonstrates: Show the confirmed preferred name as a discreet staff cue.
Evidence needed to mark: Confirmed guest match and complete interaction/audio are needed to judge natural, discreet use without overuse.

LQA standard (source wording): EFFORT - Did the employee make every effort to meet the guest's requests or offer a suitable alternative?
What the system demonstrates: Assess the staff response for effort or a suitable alternative.
Evidence needed to mark: Guest request and staff response are needed; check the service outcome when fulfillment is claimed.

LQA standard (source wording): PERSONALIZATION - Did an employee personalize the interaction in any way and engage the guest as an individual?
What the system demonstrates: Show a confirmed preference so staff can tailor the interaction.
Evidence needed to mark: Authorized profile or exact guest statement plus staff response are needed to evidence personalization.

LQA standard (source wording): ACTIVE LISTENING - Did the employee actively listen, seek clarity if required, avoid interrupting and give the guest their undivided attention (i.e. the guest should not have to repeat the request)?
What the system demonstrates: Capture speaker turns and possible clarification or repetition signals.
Evidence needed to mark: Complete speaker-labelled audio is needed to assess interruptions, overlap, attention, and repeated requests.

LQA standard (source wording): EMPATHY - Where applicable, did the employee display self-control and empathy in challenging interactions and offer a suitable alternative/resolution?
What the system demonstrates: Assess the staff response, suitable alternative, and resolution in a challenging interaction.
Evidence needed to mark: Guest concern, staff response, audio/human review, and outcome are needed where relevant.
